{{Quote|She is a remarkable vessel. With the engineering breakthroughs we tackled developing her, she's just the start. She's a real sign of things to come.|Walex Blissex|<ref name="hnn">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|47|jediwatch/13314_1.html|New Jedi Starfighter Unveiled}}</ref>}}
The '''Delta-7 ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor''', more commonly known as the '''Delta-7 ''Aethersprite'' light interceptor''' or '''Jedi starfighter''' due to its extensive use by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], was an [[Interceptor/Legends|interceptor]] commissioned just before the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].

The [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] was considered highly advanced at the time of its creation and carried sophisticated equipment, but it was expensive to produce. The ship was armed with two twin laser cannons (later models modified by Jedi Master [[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]] would contain four quad-pulse laser cannons hidden behind breakaway panels, in addition to its usual complement of two twin laser cannons), and an advanced communication and sensor array kept the pilot of the ship well-prepared in firefights as well as peacetime.

The Delta-7 fighter was fairly prominent in the Clone Wars, mainly due to its use by Jedi. One of the most famous [[Dogfight over Geonosis/Legends|encounters]] and tests of the Delta-7 was the tracking of [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] by [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] through the [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] fields of [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]].

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|Beautiful ship.|[[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]]|<ref name="AotCn">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:Aethersprite-console.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Delta-7 console displaying an [[Unidentified script (Star Wars '76)|unidentified language]]]]
Due to their visual similarities, the Delta-7 appeared to be an evolutionary descendant from the ancient [[Aurek-class tactical strikefighter|''Aurek''-class starfighter]]: it was a small, sleek interceptor used by the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] for reconnaissance missions. However, the starfighter was fitted with two twin-barrel [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]] allowing the [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] to fight when necessary. As part of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic's]] [[Judicial Department/Legends|Judicial Department]], the starfighters owned by the Jedi Order were colored in the red and white hues that represented the diplomatic immunity that the Jedi enjoyed, similar to Republic Cruisers. However, some would be painted in other colors as the Clone Wars progressed.

It was designed by engineer [[Walex Blissex/Legends|Walex Blissex]], who would later design the [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter/Legends|Alpha-3 ''Nimbus''-class V-wing starfighter]] and work on the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]] with [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]]. Due to limitations in technology at the time of its creation, the starfighter's size did not allow for a built-in [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], and instead had to rely on other spacecraft or an external [[Hyperspace transport ring/Legends|hyperdrive docking ring]] for faster-than-light travel. (However, at the time of its creation, there were also some prototype Delta-7 ''Aethersprite''s constructed that had experimental hyperdrive engines built-in.<ref name="Databank Jedi Starfighter">{{DB|starship|delta7|Jedi starfighter}}</ref> In addition to this, the standard factory-model ''Aethersprite'' could be modified and/or tweaked to have a built-in hyperdrive engine<ref name="Databank Anakin Skywalker's Customized Jedi Starfighter">{{DB|starship|anakinscustomstarfighter|Jedi starfighter, Anakin Skywalker's customized}}</ref>). The ''Aethersprite'' also had very powerful sublight engines, driving it to a maximum acceleration of 5,000 G.<ref name="CCS" />

The very first models of ''Aethersprite '' would not allow for a full-size [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] navigator, as next-generation starfighters, such as the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing]], would commonly use (most likely due to the fact that, because of the ''Aethersprite's'' design and its hull's thinness, a full-size [[Astromech socket/Legends|astromech socket]] wouldn't fit). Instead, the astromech [[Droid/Legends|droids]] were integrated directly into the starfighter, with only the truncated droid's head visible. At least two models of these droids were used, the [[R3-D]], which was used primarily for targeting (needed because the starfighter was so fast that most pilots would not be able to fire correctly and/or accurately), and the [[R4-P astromech droid|R4-P]], which was used more for navigation than targeting. Later though, a newer model of ''Aethersprite'', the [[Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7B]], would allow for a factory-model astromech-droid navigator.

==History==
===Pre-Clone Wars===
{{Quote|He-ey, nice ship there, Adi! If you're thinking of selling&hellip;''"<br />"''This ship is not for sale. It is a prototype that may become a powerful aid to the Jedi.|[[Reti]] and [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]]|<ref name="SW:JS">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Jedi_Starfighter_fightmodus.jpg|thumb|right|180px|A [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] complete with [[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin's]] modifications in "fight mode".]]
The Delta-series predated the Jedi's use of the Delta-7, which began testing at around [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]], and came into service shortly before the Clone Wars. The [[Delta-6 Sprite-class starfighter]] was used around the time of the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], and the [[Delta-12 Skysprite-class|Delta-12 ''Skysprite'']] was released on the civilian market following the launch of the ''[[Outbound Flight]]'' project; it would seem that this starfighter was also tested by the Jedi as [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] flew one himself just before the launch.

[[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]], not pleased with the vessel's already impressive performance, modified a pair of the starfighters to better suit his needs. He managed to increase the starfighter's weaponry by adding four [[quad-pulse laser]] cannons to its usual complement of two dual cannons, which were fitted behind breakaway panels until the pilot chose to enter "fight mode"; this was only done when it was deemed absolutely necessary. In addition to these weapons, Tiin also managed to fit a small Class 3 hyperdrive of his own making, negating the need for a hyperdrive ring unless time was of the essence. He also replaced the regular pilot seat with a more comfortable meditation chair, allowing for a Jedi to enter into their meditations much more easily during long hyperspace journeys.

Jedi Master [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]] flight-tested one of these Delta-7 prototypes when faced with Captain [[Cavik Toth]] and his [[Trihexalon]] fleet, taking it to the [[Karthakk system]] shortly before the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]]. It was here that she also learned to use several [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]] in conjunction with the starfighter, both offensive and defensive.<ref name="SW:JS" /> The resounding success of this mission meant that many of the existing Delta-7s were modified to Tiin's specifications.

[[File:Jedi_Starfighter_AotC.png|thumb|left|250px|Front view of a Delta-7 [[Interceptor/Legends|interceptor]].]]

Obi-Wan flew the other of these prototypes on his mission to [[Albecus]], also shortly before the Battle of Geonosis, and was attacked by [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] in his [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']] en route. He managed to fight him off thanks to the hidden weaponry and continued on his journey; it seems that the next time Kenobi faced Fett, he was in a regular Delta-7. It is possible that the result would have been very different if he had been in the same prototype.

Several hues emerged due to individual customization during the Clone Wars. [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] extensively modified ''[[Azure Angel]]'', adding large turbine engines, an internal hyperdrive, and a paint scheme reminiscent of that used on [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer/Legends|his podracer]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="Jedi Trial">''[[Jedi Trial]]''</ref> Some Delta-7s even included a bomb chute in the rear or a forward [[Seismic charge/Legends|seismic charge]] launcher, although these were rare.<ref name="RSIII" />

===The Clone Wars===
[[File:Jedi_Starfighters_Kamino.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Jedi starfighters on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].]]
More extensive deviations from the standard Delta-7 also existed, and unlike Anakin's personal craft they were available in limited numbers from [[Kuat Systems Engineering/Legends|Kuat Systems Engineering]]. Jedi wishing to avoid clashes with enemy forces sometimes used a high-speed variant. This version of the fighter featured greatly enhanced acceleration as well as an increase in maximum velocity from 1,150 kilometers per hour to 1,260 kilometers per hour. On the opposite end of the spectrum, Jedi expecting to engage in heavy dog-fights would often employ the Delta-7s high-maneuver variant. Modified using advice collected from various Jedi pilots (including [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]]), the high-maneuver version of the ship was known to aggravate droid starfighters during combat.

As Delta-7s were lost in battle, they were replaced by [[Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7Bs]]. The main modification of the 7B series was that the droid socket was centered. This allowed unmodified, detachable astromechs (R2 series and higher) to be used. This move was popular amongst most Jedi, and the trait was carried on to the Eta-2s. [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]] also flew a [[Blade of Dorin/Legends|Delta-7B]].

Towards the end of the Clone Wars, manufacturer [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]] developed a more refined starfighter&mdash; the [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class interceptor]]&mdash; based on experience gained from the Delta-7 ''Aethersprite''. These fighters were used in large numbers during the Clone Wars, including the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]]. A number of Delta-7 starfighters remained in use by the Jedi after the introduction of the Eta-2, including Plo Koon's [[Plo Koon's Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|personal starfighter]], as he preferred the Delta-7 to the point that he continued to use it until [[Order 66/Legends|his death]] at [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]]. Several years after the Clone Wars ended, Kuat sold the entire Delta line to [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]]. Afterwards, the Delta-7 would be phased out.

===Galactic Civil War===
Most Delta-7s were lost in action during the Clone Wars, and many that survived have languished for decades in hangars and scrapyards throughout the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].<ref name="Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook">[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]]</ref> [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] would later retrieve an abandoned Delta-7 after his X-Wing crash-landed on Geonosis sometime after the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] in the [[Battle of Geonosis (Galactic Civil War)|Third Battle of Geonosis]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. As he needed a way to escape the planet after being attacked by a [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|Republic gunship]] piloted by [[Sarkli]], the exterior was relatively undamaged, and his R5 unit repowered it. Afterwards, he utilized its [[Void-7 seismic charge/Legends|Void-7 seismic charges]] to destroy two Storm Commando-owned [[Imperial escort carrier (storm commando)|Imperial escort carriers]], and also eliminating several squadrons of [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|Tie bombers]], [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|Tie Interceptors]], and [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|Tie fighters]] before promptly retreating alongside the Rebels via a hyperspace ring. It was later stored in a starfighter hangar.<ref name="RSIII">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

The design of the Delta-7 later evolved into the [[R-22 Spearhead starfighter|R-22 Spearhead]] and the [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]] of the Galactic Civil War.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:JediStarfighter-ConceptArt.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Concept art by [[Doug Chiang]]]]
Delta-7 ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptors first appeared in [[2002]] with the release of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] and its tie-ins.

The starfighter was originally conceived as a "Stormtrooper Fighter", which would have linked both the [[Prequel trilogy|Prequel]] and [[Original trilogy|Original]] trilogies together.<ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref>

Jedi starfighters appear in the [[2002]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''. They are the Galactic Republic special units and are produced at Fortresses.

In [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] Obi-Wan's starfighter's in-cockpit display screen displays information using the [[Unidentified script (Star Wars '76)|Star Wars '76]] script, not [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]].
